result:
The import hint now walks people through putting the plan in its own calendar, and the exported file carries the plan's name. All the tests pass on temporary copies of the project, and a screenshot of the plans page looks right. The real database (same size and timestamp before and after this change) and the login and signup templates are untouched. I still haven't imported a file into Google Calendar itself, and the steps follow your wording, so please try them once.

**The hint under each plan's buttons now reads:**

> To import the exported file into its own calendar, which you can tick on or off:
> 1. In Google Calendar, go to Settings > Add calendar > Create new calendar, and name it "Half marathon plan (Jan 31, 2027)".
> 2. Go to Settings > Import & export, choose the exported file, and pick that new calendar under "Add to calendar".
>
> To remove the plan later, delete that calendar.

**Things to check**
- **The plan's name is my choice:** plans don't have a name field, so I built one from the distance and race date. The date keeps two plans for the same distance apart.
- **The calendar name in the file may not be used by Google:** I added it as `X-WR-CALNAME`, a widely used but non-standard field. As far as I know, Google ignores it on import, which is why the hint gives the exact name to type. Other calendar apps may use it.
- **The hint is now left-aligned:** a numbered list read badly right-aligned, so this is one small change beyond the wording. It also repeats on every plan, because each plan needs its own name. If that feels long with several plans, it could collapse behind a "How to import" toggle.

**Files changed:**
- `plans.html`: the hint text
- `style.css`: the hint's layout
- `plan_generator.py`: the calendar name in the file
- `main.py`: the plan name, used by both the hint and the file
